text:
Buck is a big, good-natured dog, half St. Bernard and half Scotch shepherd, who has spent his four years as the favourite of Judge Miller's sunny estate in California's Santa Clara Valley. In the autumn of 1897 gold has been found in the far north, and the men rushing to the Klondike need strong dogs to haul their sleds. One evening a gardener with gambling debts quietly leads Buck away and sells him to strangers.

Caged, beaten and carried north by train and steamer, Buck learns his first hard lesson from a man in a red sweater who carries a club, and comes ashore at Dyea among sled dogs, snow and men who live by rules he has never known. Jack London's short novel follows a pampered house dog thrown into the work and the dangers of the Yukon trail.
